title: Scoped negative result: fixed P112 24-row boundary retains COPY64
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**Scoped negative result with a written proof and exact finite premises; no new supplier or kappa.** PR #1375 leaves its first free-compatible 24-row span-loss boundary open. This package proves that this exact boundary still has sharp whole-decoder COPY cost **64**, for arbitrary complex correction amplitudes (including zeros), arbitrary singleton amplitude, and every GL(3,C) mixing with the two specified coordinate modes.

The replacement ranks either include two ranks at least eight, or are all at least seven. Thus their separate power bill is at least `2*8^q` for every `0<q<=1`. The cancellation-aligned example changes `(8,8,0)` into `(7,8,7)`: reducing one term raises the whole bill to 70. Omitting its compensation fails a constrained entry. Identity mixing attains 64, including a rank-nine masked completion.

Only `research/p112-boundary24-seed39/` is added. Larger rectangles, other supports, more mixed modes, shared-copy billing and physical realization remain outside scope. No full child histogram, moment improvement, all-size compiler, precision/hosting invoice or multiplication theorem is claimed.

## Task and overlap

- Base: `bce54fb3f895cbe5cd4c0eb477c3afeed100190f`; contribution: `4bcc49e3f4041018b0607da46a87d8928a6e0fd0`.
- OS-random seed **39**, complex-supplier track. Task `complex-masked-decoder`, scope **refined** to the fixed PR1375 boundary. The initial aligned-amplitude question extends to arbitrary amplitudes on the same support through the proof, not a larger search.
- Predecessor PR #1375: `4a533aff2a7a87c9b36e077a31774b332a7f64bd`. Its support cap 23 does not cover the full named boundary. Its theorem is not assumed: all new finite premises are recomputed.
- PR #1331: `f08b698cc2bd74e2425486728a008e531fc35f0e`, the one-coordinate predecessor and two-coordinate handoff. Discussion #1360 concerns all nine factors of a singleton-by-singleton completion; this package treats a 24-by-one correction with two original modes mixed.
- [Claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1316#discussioncomment-18912070). The final recorded overlap scan completely paginated 788 open PRs and 146 discussion records without warnings. Another agent listed this boundary as a candidate but chose a different investigation.
- Refreshed main `410026dc5513b87db92ae98571d1d5984c69a983` preserves all four source pins; the patch applies cleanly. Selected frontier and frozen sources are unchanged.

## Validation

Python 3.12.13, standard library only:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-boundary24-seed39
```

Expected: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/p112-boundary24-seed39 outcome=negative-result`.

The primary implementation checks **655** exact support pairings, **9** Gaussian-rational full matrix fixtures (**112,896 entries**) and **9 controls**. A separate implementation imports neither primary nor predecessor code, rebuilds Euclidean E8 geometry, rechecks every finite premise with set-based binary elimination, and checks **25,088** integer identities, two nonzero rank-nine minors and **6 controls**.

The registered replay, both optimized-mode checkers, read-only relocated replay, five external corrupted-source/receipt rejection runs, 20 repository workflow tests, selected-record integrity and whitespace check pass. The scoped quantified argument is written in the README; finite replay is not formal verification. Native/Lean builds, hosted CI and the full selected-supplier cold replay were not run locally.

## Credit

Credit commdata2338 / PR1375 for the explicit boundary and question; Arham Tahir / PR1331 for the earlier handoff; Mihir Srivastava / PR845 for the pinned geometry; DreamingOfClouds / PR717 and PR446/595 for the framework; themilkman216 / PR968 for the pairing-cost model; Joel Pulikkan / GamingPuzzled / PR620 for COPY64; and woklerx / PR1077 for the orientation check.

Prepared for **Hanson Sun / bbMisk** with substantial **OpenAI Codex** assistance in mathematics, code, verification and writing. Both implementations have the same AI-assisted author; no independent human review is claimed. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

The [package README](https://github.com/bbMisk/integer-mult-bounds/blob/4bcc49e3f4041018b0607da46a87d8928a6e0fd0/research/p112-boundary24-seed39/README.md#open-next-questions) identifies two bounded extensions: another maximal free rectangle, or three original modes on this U. First compute the relevant survivor/pure-correction pairings and coupled power bill. The present singleton case split and two-mode geometry do not settle either question.
